chapter: Cab Calloway's band, Hadacol and closing reflections
title: Closing thanks and the fiftieth anniversary
summary: Milt thanks the National Foundation, explains why he asked about genealogy, and Lu notes it is their fiftieth anniversary year.

story.theme_name: Thanks and goodbyes: closing the interview
story.community_name: Closing thanks and goodbyes at the end of the interview

blocks.x: This is forever. I want to thank you. And I want to thank the National Foundation for even having the opportunity to do this with you. Because this is for posterity. And there's not enough of this done to let the world know about what has happened and how this thing, this American art form... And what a great part you and Danny are of this thing! And that's one of the reasons why I had you talk about that genealogy, to show how interconnected you are with all the Jazz in this New Orleans area.

And New Orleans is a great city, and you're doing lots of Jazz still, and lots of American music down here. I mean, this Festival is a monumental thing. More should be done in other cities like this, and more recognition should be given to the people who are the forerunners, who are responsible for it being here, and turning you on, telling guys like Paul Barbarin, your late uncle and all of these
great people, Bunk Johnson and...without even a mention... We didn't even mention Louis, because everybody mentions Louis Armstrong.
We all know about Louis, and we know what a master he is. And I just wanted to talk to you, Danny. Now, what are you doing now? What's that, Lu?
This year we've been married fifty years. And this was made for that.
Isn't that beautiful. Fifty years of marriage.
And this is the wedding ring...
Oh, that's what we have, two wedding rings. "To Lu Barker and Daniel Barker..."
And (?) and two wedding rings on the fifty years of marriage...

"From January 8, 1930 to..." Oh, isn't this beautiful, still here. "Larry, Kelly and Christopher and Linda." Isn't that beautiful? This is just lovely. Well, congratulations. And I hope we can just go right on into that century mark together! [LAUGHS] I laugh at these young people and what they do.
